title: Habitats, Populations and Communities
seo_title: Primary 6 Science: Habitats, Populations and Communities Worksheets (PSLE Practice)
standard_code: Primary 6: Interactions within the environment (Habitats, populations and communities)
standard_text: Recognise that a habitat is the place where an organism lives, a population is a group of one kind of organism living in a habitat, and a community is all the populations living together in a habitat. Investigate how environmental factors (light, temperature, water and air) affect the distribution of organisms (summary of the MOE Primary Science Syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Primary 6 science worksheets for Singapore pupils on habitats, populations and communities: counting populations, environmental factors and fair experiments. PSLE practice with answers.
key_big: One kind = population. All kinds = community.
key_sub: A habitat is the place where they live.
body_html:
How to think about it

A habitat is where an organism lives. A population is one kind of organism there. A community is all the populations living together.

  • One guppy is an organism. All the guppies in the pond are a population.
  • All the plants and animals in the pond together are a community. Water and soil are not part of it.
  • Environmental factors: light, temperature, water and air. They affect where organisms live.
  • Organisms in a community depend on each other for food, shelter and pollination.
Example

A pond has guppies, snails and water lilies. How many populations are there?

Count the kinds of organisms

Answer: 3

Example

Earthworms move to the damp side of a box. Which factor affects them?

Only water changes

Answer: the amount of water

Common mistakes

  • Calling all the animals in a habitat a population. A population is one kind only.
  • Leaving plants out of a community. Plants are populations too.
  • Putting water, soil or rocks in a community. A community is only living things.
  • Changing two factors at once in an experiment.

faq.q: What is the difference between a population and a community?
faq.a: A population is one kind of organism in a habitat. A community is all the populations living there together.

faq.q: Is the water in a pond part of the community?
faq.a: No. A community is only the living things. Water is part of the habitat.
Light, temperature, water and air affect where organisms can live and how many there are.

items.q: Which statement about a habitat is correct?
c: A habitat provides food, water, shelter and air for organisms.
A habitat has only one kind of organism.
Organisms do not need a habitat.
A habitat is always very large.
items.e: Habitats can be big (a forest) or small (a rotting log).

items.q: Which of these is not part of a community?

items.e: Water is non-living; a community is only living things.
